text.p: Seventeen people, most believed to be Ukrainian women, died in a fire that broke out at a hotel in central Istanbul early on Sunday, police officials said.
The lower floors of the hotel were gutted by the blaze which broke out around 4.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) in a shop on the ground floor of a hotel in Istanbul's Laleli district, television reports said.

They said most of the dead and injured were Ukrainian women, poisoned by smoke inhalation. A police officer told Reuters 39 people were known to have been injured in the fire in the seven-storey, three star hotel.
Television pictures showed the injured, their faces blackened by smoke, climbing out of hotel windows and clambering down fire engine ladders.
A group of 65 Ukrainians who arrived in Istanbul three days earlier was staying in the 60-room hotel, one of the group told state-run Anatolian news agency.

"Why didn't the hotel staff wake us when the fire broke out? When the fire started, they ran away. That's why our friends were stuck in the lobby," said Natalia Tcherninova, who escaped through a window with help from fire services.

Tourism Minister Bahattin Yucel told reporters at the scene the deaths occurred as hotel residents crowded into the smoke-filled lobby. He said police were cooperating with the Ukrainian consulate in identifying the victims, but said the process had not been completed.
Traders from eastern Europe involved in Istanbul's widespread "suitcase trade" stay in hotels in the crowded Laleli area of the city.
Istanbul city fire chief Muhittin Sogukoglu rejected earlier reports that the fire was caused by a gas leak or arson.
"We are concentrating on the electricity system as the cause of the fire," he was quoted as saying by Anatolian.

Fire services quickly brought the blaze under control and the injured were taken to nearby hospitals. Hospital officials said 14 of the dead were women and that some of the injured were in a critical condition.
